## Classes

### <a name="certmanager"></a>`certmanager`

Wraps certbot, DigiCert CertCentral and a self-signed issuer behind one
resource shape, lands everything in one canonical store, reports on it
through a fact, and wires consuming services in so they reload when a
certificate changes.

Including this class on its own does nothing except create the store and
set up the fact cache. Certificates come from `certmanager::certificate`,
or from the `certificates` parameter if you would rather declare them in
Hiera.

#### Examples

##### Let's Encrypt with DNS validation

```puppet
class { 'certmanager':
  default_issuer => 'letsencrypt',
  issuers        => {
    'letsencrypt' => {
      'backend'                 => 'acme',
      'directory_url'           => 'https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory',
      'email'                   => 'certs@example.com',
      'challenge'               => 'dns-01',
      'dns_plugin'              => 'cloudflare',
      'dns_credentials'         => Sensitive('dns_cloudflare_api_token = ...'),
      'dns_propagation_seconds' => 60,
    },
  },
}
```

##### Finding the certificates nobody put in Puppet

```puppet
class { 'certmanager':
  scan_directories => ['/etc/pki/tls/certs', '/opt/app/ssl'],
  scan_recursive   => true,
}
```

## Defined types

### <a name="certmanager--certificate"></a>`certmanager::certificate`

The resource you actually declare. Resolves the issuer configuration,
plants a bootstrap placeholder so dependent services can start before the
real certificate exists, and hands the issuance itself to the
`certmanager_certificate` resource.

#### Examples

##### A wildcard through DNS validation

```puppet
certmanager::certificate { 'star.example.com':
  issuer      => 'letsencrypt',
  common_name => '*.example.com',
  san         => ['example.com'],
  challenge   => 'dns-01',
}
```

##### A DigiCert certificate for the thing the auditors care about

```puppet
certmanager::certificate { 'payments.example.com':
  issuer            => 'digicert',
  san               => ['payments-api.example.com'],
  key_type          => 'rsa-3072',
  renew_before_days => 45,
}
```

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['present', 'absent']`

`present` issues and renews. `absent` revokes with the CA, and deletes
the files only if `purge` is also set.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--issuer"></a>`issuer`

Data type: `Optional[Certmanager::Issuer]`

Which issuer instance signs this certificate. Defaults to
`certmanager::default_issuer`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--common_name"></a>`common_name`

Data type: `Optional[Certmanager::Dnsname]`

Subject common name. Defaults to the resource title, which is what you
want unless the title is a nickname rather than a hostname.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--san"></a>`san`

Data type: `Array[Certmanager::Dnsname]`

Additional DNS names. The common name is added automatically, so there
is no need to repeat it here.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--key_type"></a>`key_type`

Data type: `Certmanager::Keytype`

Private key algorithm and size. Changing it reissues the certificate.

Default value: `'ecdsa-p256'`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--renew_before_days"></a>`renew_before_days`

Data type: `Integer[1, 365]`

Days before expiry at which renewal is attempted. The default of 30 is
Let's Encrypt's own recommendation and leaves a fortnight of failed
runs before anything actually breaks.

Default value: `30`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--challenge"></a>`challenge`

Data type: `Optional[Certmanager::Challenge]`

ACME challenge type, overriding the issuer's default. `dns-01` is the
only one that issues wildcards and the only one that does not need the
host reachable from the internet.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--webroot"></a>`webroot`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::Absolutepath]`

Document root for `http-01`, overriding the issuer's default.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--subject"></a>`subject`

Data type: `Hash[Enum['O', 'OU', 'C', 'ST', 'L'], String[1]]`

Additional subject components (O, OU, C, ST, L). Public CAs ignore most
of these; DigiCert takes them from the organisation record instead.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--pkcs12_password"></a>`pkcs12_password`

Data type: `Optional[Certmanager::Secret]`

Password for the PKCS#12 bundle. Omit and no bundle is generated, which
is the right answer unless something downstream wants a keystore.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--bootstrap"></a>`bootstrap`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to plant a self-signed placeholder when the store is empty.
Leave this on unless you validate through DNS and nothing depends on
the certificate file existing before first issuance.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--bootstrap_validity_days"></a>`bootstrap_validity_days`

Data type: `Integer[1, 3650]`

How long the placeholder is valid for. Short on purpose: a placeholder
nobody noticed should set off an alert in a fortnight, not serve
production for a year.

Default value: `30`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--purge"></a>`purge`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether `ensure => absent` deletes the key material as well as revoking
it. Off by default, because removing a certificate from a manifest is
usually a refactor and losing the key to one is not recoverable.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--force_renewal"></a>`force_renewal`

Data type: `Boolean`

Reissue on the next run regardless of the renewal window. Not
idempotent, by definition. Use the `certmanager::renew` task instead
unless you genuinely want this in a manifest.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-certmanager--certificate--revocation_reason"></a>`revocation_reason`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Reason passed to the CA on revocation.

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="certmanager--consumer"></a>`certmanager::consumer`

There are two renewal paths and they need different handling, which is
why this is one resource doing two jobs rather than two resources.

On a Puppet run, `Certmanager_certificate` notifies the service directly.
That is what covers first issuance and anything Puppet itself changed.

Between Puppet runs, certbot renews on its own timer and Puppet never
sees it. So this also writes a deploy hook script, which the ACME backend
invokes after any out-of-band renewal. Without it a certificate renews
perfectly and the service carries on serving the old one until the next
Puppet run happens to notice.

The service relationship uses a collector, so declaring a consumer for a
service managed in some other module (or not managed at all) does not
fail compilation.

#### Examples

##### nginx, the common case

```puppet
certmanager::consumer { 'nginx-www':
  certificate => 'www.example.com',
  service     => 'nginx',
}
```

##### A service that wants its own copy of the key

```puppet
certmanager::consumer { 'postfix-mail':
  certificate    => 'mail.example.com',
  service        => 'postfix',
  commands       => [
    'install -o postfix -g postfix -m 0600 "$CERTMANAGER_PRIVKEY" /etc/postfix/tls/key.pem',
    'install -o root -g root -m 0644 "$CERTMANAGER_FULLCHAIN" /etc/postfix/tls/cert.pem',
  ],
  reload_command => 'systemctl reload postfix',
  only_if        => 'systemctl is-active --quiet postfix',
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `certmanager::consumer` defined type:

* [`certificate`](#-certmanager--consumer--certificate)
* [`ensure`](#-certmanager--consumer--ensure)
* [`service`](#-certmanager--consumer--service)
* [`reload_command`](#-certmanager--consumer--reload_command)
* [`commands`](#-certmanager--consumer--commands)
* [`only_if`](#-certmanager--consumer--only_if)
* [`manage_relationship`](#-certmanager--consumer--manage_relationship)

##### <a name="-certmanager--consumer--certificate"></a>`certificate`

Data type: `Certmanager::Certname`

Name of the certificate this service uses, matching the
`certmanager::certificate` title.

##### <a name="-certmanager--consumer--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['present', 'absent']`

Whether the hook exists.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-certmanager--consumer--service"></a>`service`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Service resource to notify on a Puppet-driven change. Omit if nothing
in this catalog manages the service.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-certmanager--consumer--reload_command"></a>`reload_command`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Command the out-of-band hook runs to make the service pick up the new
certificate. Defaults to reloading `service` through systemctl on
Linux, or `Restart-Service` on Windows.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-certmanager--consumer--commands"></a>`commands`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Extra commands the hook runs before the reload. This is where a service
that insists on its own copy of the certificate, with its own
ownership, gets one.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-certmanager--consumer--only_if"></a>`only_if`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Guard command. The hook exits 0 without doing anything when this is
false, so a stopped service does not produce a failed hook that buries
the real ones.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-certmanager--consumer--manage_relationship"></a>`manage_relationship`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to wire the Puppet-run ordering and notification. Turn this off
if you want to declare the relationships yourself.

Default value: `true`

## Resource types

### <a name="certmanager_certificate"></a>`certmanager_certificate`

This is the resource that actually talks to a CA. It is not usually
declared directly: `certmanager::certificate` wraps it, resolves the
issuer configuration out of Hiera, sets up the store directories and
wires in the consumers.

A certificate is not a conventional resource. Whether it is "correct"
depends on the clock and on the names it carries, not on simple
presence, so the provider compares four things on every run: the
certificate exists, it is not inside its renewal window, its SAN list
matches what was declared, and its key type matches what was declared.
Any of those failing triggers reissue.

#### Examples

##### An ACME certificate with two names

```puppet
certmanager_certificate { 'www.example.com':
  ensure        => present,
  issuer        => 'letsencrypt',
  issuer_config => $config,
  common_name   => 'www.example.com',
  san           => ['example.com'],
  key_type      => 'ecdsa-p256',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `certmanager_certificate` type.

##### `certificate_state`

Data type: `Enum[current, renewal_due, placeholder, missing, unreadable]`

        Whether the certificate on disk is still fit for purpose.

        Always declared as `current`; the provider reports what it actually
        found. This is what makes time-based renewal work: an expiring
        certificate shows as drift in the report rather than silently
        staying "present" until the day it breaks.

        `placeholder` means the bootstrap self-signed certificate is still
        in place and real issuance has not succeeded.

Default value: `current`

##### `days_left`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Whole days until expiry. Negative once expired.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the certificate should exist in the store.

Default value: `present`

##### `fingerprint_sha256`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

SHA-256 fingerprint of the DER encoding.

##### `key_type`

Data type: `Enum[ecdsa-p256, ecdsa-p384, ecdsa-p521, rsa-2048, rsa-3072, rsa-4096]`

Private key algorithm and size. Changing it triggers reissue.

Default value: `ecdsa-p256`

##### `not_after`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Expiry timestamp, ISO 8601 UTC.

##### `san`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Every DNS name on the certificate, sorted. Adding or removing one triggers reissue.

Default value: `[]`

##### `serial`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Certificate serial number, hex.

##### <a name="-certmanager_certificate--issuer"></a>`issuer`

##### <a name="-certmanager_certificate--purge_on_absent"></a>`purge_on_absent`

Data type: `Boolean`

##### <a name="-certmanager_certificate--renew_before_days"></a>`renew_before_days`

Data type: `Integer[1, 365]`

        renewal. The default of 30 is Let's Encrypt's own recommendation and
        leaves room for a fortnight of failed runs before anything breaks.

Default value: `30`

##### <a name="-certmanager_certificate--revocation_reason"></a>`revocation_reason`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Reason passed to the CA when revoking.

##### <a name="-certmanager_certificate--subject"></a>`subject`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], String[1]]`

Additional subject components (O, OU, C, ST, L).

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-certmanager_certificate--webroot"></a>`webroot`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Document root for http-01 validation, overriding the issuer default.

### <a name="certmanager_placeholder"></a>`certmanager_placeholder`

Exists to break the first-run deadlock. nginx will not start without a
certificate file, an `http-01` challenge cannot succeed without a web
server answering, and the certificate does not exist until the challenge
succeeds. Three things each waiting on the other.

This resource writes a short-lived self-signed certificate into the
store if, and only if, the store is empty. It never overwrites a real
certificate: replacing a valid public certificate with a self-signed one
as a side effect of a Puppet run would be considerably worse than the
problem it solves.

Order it before the consuming service and let `certmanager_certificate`
notify that service once the real certificate lands:

```puppet
Certmanager_placeholder['www.example.com'] -> Service['nginx']
Certmanager_certificate['www.example.com'] ~> Service['nginx']
```

The `certmanager` fact reports a placeholder as `self_signed` and lists
it under `placeholders`, so a certificate stuck on its bootstrap is
visible rather than quietly serving a certificate nobody trusts.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `certmanager_placeholder` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

        Normally left alone. A placeholder is created when the store is
        empty and then replaced by the real certificate.

        `absent` removes a placeholder that is still a placeholder. It will
        not remove a real certificate that has since replaced one, because
        deleting a working certificate as a side effect of tidying up a
        bootstrap would be a spectacular own goal.

Default value: `present`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `certmanager_placeholder` type.

* [`common_name`](#-certmanager_placeholder--common_name)
* [`key_type`](#-certmanager_placeholder--key_type)
* [`name`](#-certmanager_placeholder--name)
* [`san`](#-certmanager_placeholder--san)
* [`subject`](#-certmanager_placeholder--subject)
* [`validity_days`](#-certmanager_placeholder--validity_days)

##### <a name="-certmanager_placeholder--common_name"></a>`common_name`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Subject common name. Defaults to the resource title.

##### <a name="-certmanager_placeholder--key_type"></a>`key_type`

Data type: `Enum[ecdsa-p256, ecdsa-p384, ecdsa-p521, rsa-2048, rsa-3072, rsa-4096]`

Key type for the placeholder. Matching the real certificate avoids a needless key change on issuance.

Default value: `ecdsa-p256`

##### <a name="-certmanager_placeholder--name"></a>`name`

namevar

Data type: `String[1]`

Certificate name, matching the certmanager_certificate it bootstraps.

##### <a name="-certmanager_placeholder--san"></a>`san`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

DNS names to put on the placeholder, so a virtual host matching on SNI still works.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-certmanager_placeholder--subject"></a>`subject`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], String[1]]`

Additional subject components.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-certmanager_placeholder--validity_days"></a>`validity_days`

Data type: `Integer[1, 3650]`

        How long the placeholder is valid for. Short on purpose: a
        placeholder that outlives its welcome is a placeholder nobody
        noticed, and a monitoring alert in a fortnight is better than a
        self-signed certificate serving production for a year.

Default value: `30`

## Functions

### <a name="certmanager--expiring"></a>`certmanager::expiring`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

Certificates on this node expiring within the given number of days.

Reads the `certmanager` fact, so it reports on everything the inventory
knows about, not only what this catalog declares. That distinction is the
point: the certificate about to expire is usually the one nobody put in
Puppet.

#### Examples

##### Fail a run when something is about to break

```puppet
$doomed = certmanager::expiring(7)
unless empty($doomed) {
  notify { "certificates expiring within 7 days: ${join($doomed, ', ')}": }
}
```

#### `certmanager::expiring(Optional[Integer[0]] $days)`

Certificates on this node expiring within the given number of days.

Reads the `certmanager` fact, so it reports on everything the inventory
knows about, not only what this catalog declares. That distinction is the
point: the certificate about to expire is usually the one nobody put in
Puppet.

Returns: `Array[String]` Certificate names, soonest first.

##### Examples

###### Fail a run when something is about to break

```puppet
$doomed = certmanager::expiring(7)
unless empty($doomed) {
  notify { "certificates expiring within 7 days: ${join($doomed, ', ')}": }
}
```

##### `days`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0]]`

How far ahead to look.

### <a name="certmanager--module_libdir"></a>`certmanager::module_libdir`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

The path to this module's own `lib` directory in the current environment.

Needed because the deploy hook and the fact-cache refresh job are plain
Ruby scripts run outside any Puppet run, so they have to be told where the
module's libraries are. On an agent, pluginsync has already copied them
into the vardir and that is the answer. Under `puppet apply` it has not,
and this is.

Returns undef when the module cannot be located, which is the normal case
when the catalogue was compiled on a server: the server's module path
means nothing on the agent, and the vardir copy is the right answer there
anyway.

#### `certmanager::module_libdir()`

The path to this module's own `lib` directory in the current environment.

Needed because the deploy hook and the fact-cache refresh job are plain
Ruby scripts run outside any Puppet run, so they have to be told where the
module's libraries are. On an agent, pluginsync has already copied them
into the vardir and that is the answer. Under `puppet apply` it has not,
and this is.

Returns undef when the module cannot be located, which is the normal case
when the catalogue was compiled on a server: the server's module path
means nothing on the agent, and the vardir copy is the right answer there
anyway.

### <a name="certmanager--path"></a>`certmanager::path`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

Returns the canonical path to one file of a managed certificate.

This is how consuming configuration finds a certificate without hardcoding
a path that is correct only for one issuer. An nginx template calls this
and keeps working when the certificate moves from Let's Encrypt to
DigiCert, because the store layout does not change.

The location honours `certmanager::store_dir` from Hiera, so overriding
the store in data moves the function's answer with it.

#### Examples

##### In an EPP template

```puppet
ssl_certificate     <%= certmanager::path($cert, 'fullchain') %>;
ssl_certificate_key <%= certmanager::path($cert, 'privkey') %>;
```

#### `certmanager::path(Certmanager::Certname $name, Optional[Enum['cert', 'chain', 'fullchain', 'privkey', 'combined', 'pkcs12', 'metadata', 'dir']] $component)`

Returns the canonical path to one file of a managed certificate.

This is how consuming configuration finds a certificate without hardcoding
a path that is correct only for one issuer. An nginx template calls this
and keeps working when the certificate moves from Let's Encrypt to
DigiCert, because the store layout does not change.

The location honours `certmanager::store_dir` from Hiera, so overriding
the store in data moves the function's answer with it.

Returns: `Stdlib::Absolutepath` Absolute path to that file.

##### Examples

###### In an EPP template

```puppet
ssl_certificate     <%= certmanager::path($cert, 'fullchain') %>;
ssl_certificate_key <%= certmanager::path($cert, 'privkey') %>;
```

##### `name`

Data type: `Certmanager::Certname`

The certificate name, matching the `certmanager::certificate` title.

##### `component`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['cert', 'chain', 'fullchain', 'privkey', 'combined', 'pkcs12', 'metadata', 'dir']]`

Which file in the store to return.

### <a name="Certmanager--Acmeconfig"></a>`Certmanager::Acmeconfig`

Configuration for an ACME issuer instance (certbot or win-acme).

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
    backend                           => Enum['acme'],
    directory_url                     => String[1],
    email                             => Optional[String[1]],
    Optional[challenge]               => Certmanager::Challenge,
    Optional[dns_plugin]              => String[1],
    Optional[dns_credentials]         => Certmanager::Secret,
    Optional[dns_propagation_seconds] => Integer[0, 3600],
    Optional[webroot]                 => Stdlib::Absolutepath,
    Optional[eab_kid]                 => String[1],
    Optional[eab_hmac_key]            => Certmanager::Secret,
    Optional[server_port]             => Stdlib::Port,
    Optional[preferred_chain]         => String[1],
    Optional[config_dir]              => Stdlib::Absolutepath,
    Optional[certbot_path]            => String[1],
    Optional[wacs_path]               => String[1],
}]
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `Certmanager::Acmeconfig` data type:

* [`backend`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--backend)
* [`directory_url`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--directory_url)
* [`email`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--email)
* [`challenge`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--challenge)
* [`dns_plugin`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--dns_plugin)
* [`dns_credentials`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--dns_credentials)
* [`dns_propagation_seconds`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--dns_propagation_seconds)
* [`webroot`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--webroot)
* [`eab_kid`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--eab_kid)
* [`eab_hmac_key`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--eab_hmac_key)
* [`server_port`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--server_port)
* [`preferred_chain`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--preferred_chain)
* [`config_dir`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--config_dir)
* [`certbot_path`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--certbot_path)
* [`wacs_path`](#-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--wacs_path)

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--backend"></a>`backend`

Always `acme` for this shape.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--directory_url"></a>`directory_url`

The ACME directory endpoint. Let's Encrypt production and staging,
ZeroSSL, Buypass and DigiCert's own ACME service all work here.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--email"></a>`email`

Contact address registered with the CA. Expiry warnings go here.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--challenge"></a>`challenge`

Default challenge type for certificates issued by this issuer.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--dns_plugin"></a>`dns_plugin`

certbot DNS plugin name (`cloudflare`, `route53`, `rfc2136`, ...) when
`challenge` is `dns-01`. Ignored otherwise.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--dns_credentials"></a>`dns_credentials`

Credential file contents for the DNS plugin. Written 0600.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--dns_propagation_seconds"></a>`dns_propagation_seconds`

How long to wait for the DNS record to propagate before asking the CA to
validate. Too low is the single most common cause of dns-01 failures.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--webroot"></a>`webroot`

Document root for `http-01` when the web server is already running.
Omit to let the backend stand up its own listener.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--eab_kid"></a>`eab_kid`

External Account Binding key identifier, required by ZeroSSL, DigiCert
ACME and most commercial ACME endpoints.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--eab_hmac_key"></a>`eab_hmac_key`

External Account Binding HMAC key.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--server_port"></a>`server_port`

Port for the standalone challenge listener.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--preferred_chain"></a>`preferred_chain`

Issuer common name of the preferred chain, when the CA offers more than
one (the ISRG X1 / DST Root cross-sign problem).

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--config_dir"></a>`config_dir`

certbot's configuration directory, where it keeps account state and its
own `live` and `renewal-hooks` trees. Only worth setting if you run
certbot somewhere other than `/etc/letsencrypt`.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--certbot_path"></a>`certbot_path`

Path to certbot for this issuer specifically. Normally comes from
`certmanager::certbot_path` and does not need setting here.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Acmeconfig--wacs_path"></a>`wacs_path`

Path to wacs.exe for this issuer specifically. Normally comes from
`certmanager::wacs_path`.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Certinfo--issuer"></a>`issuer`

Name of the issuer instance that produced it, or `unknown` for scanned

True for a self-signed certificate. On a managed certificate this almost

`certmanager::consumer`.

### <a name="Certmanager--Certname"></a>`Certmanager::Certname`

Usually an FQDN, but it is only an identifier: the actual names on the
certificate come from `common_name` and `san`. Constrained to characters
that are safe as a directory name on both POSIX and Windows.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._*-]{0,252}\z/]`

### <a name="Certmanager--Challenge"></a>`Certmanager::Challenge`

`dns-01` is the only one that works for wildcards, and the only one that
doesn't need the host to be reachable from the internet.

Alias of `Enum['http-01', 'dns-01', 'tls-alpn-01']`

```puppet
    Optional[auto_renew_days] => Integer[1, 365],

}]
```

* [`product_name_id`](#-Certmanager--Digicertconfig--product_name_id)

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Digicertconfig--api_key"></a>`api_key`

CertCentral API key.

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Digicertconfig--product_name_id"></a>`product_name_id`

##### <a name="-Certmanager--Digicertconfig--signature_hash"></a>`signature_hash`

Hash algorithm requested for the signature.

### <a name="Certmanager--Dnsname"></a>`Certmanager::Dnsname`

A DNS name that can appear in a certificate, including wildcards.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A(\*\.)?([a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,63}\z/]`

### <a name="Certmanager--Issuer"></a>`Certmanager::Issuer`

Issuers are declared in `certmanager::issuers` and resolved at catalog
compile time. The three built-in backends are `acme`, `digicert` and
`selfsigned`; the value here is the *instance* name, so you can have several
ACME issuers (staging and production, for example) side by side.

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*\z/]`

### <a name="Certmanager--Issuerconfig"></a>`Certmanager::Issuerconfig`

Discriminated on the `backend` key, so Puppet validates the right set of
parameters for the backend you actually asked for rather than accepting a
soup of optional keys.

Alias of `Variant[Certmanager::Acmeconfig, Certmanager::Digicertconfig, Certmanager::Selfsignedconfig]`

### <a name="Certmanager--Keytype"></a>`Certmanager::Keytype`

ECDSA is the sane default in 2026. RSA is here for the load balancer that
still hasn't been replaced.

Alias of `Enum['ecdsa-p256', 'ecdsa-p384', 'rsa-2048', 'rsa-3072', 'rsa-4096']`

## Tasks

### <a name="refresh_facts"></a>`refresh_facts`

Rebuild the cache behind the certmanager fact

**Supports noop?** false

### <a name="renew"></a>`renew`

Renew a managed certificate now, without waiting for the renewal window

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `certificate`

Data type: `String[1]`

Certificate name, as it appears in the store

##### `force`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Renew even if the certificate is nowhere near expiry. Counts against the CA's rate limits.

##### `api_key`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

DigiCert CertCentral API key. Only needed for certificates issued by the digicert backend.

##### `config_dir`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

certbot configuration directory, if the issuer does not use the default

##### `organization_id`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1]]`

DigiCert organisation ID. Only needed for the digicert backend.

##### `api_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

DigiCert CertCentral API base, for the EU endpoint or a proxy

### <a name="report"></a>`report`

Report on every certificate this node knows about, managed or not

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `refresh`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Rebuild the inventory before reporting instead of reading the cache

##### `expiring_within`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[0]]`

Only report certificates expiring within this many days

##### `managed_only`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Only report certificates this module issued
